summary: This program builds a list of farmers' market products and then uses three stream pipelines to reshape that data: one collects the unique vendor names, one formats a single vendor's items as a printable menu, and one recomputes that vendor's prices with a 10% discount. It shows how `map` turns a stream of objects into a stream of something else entirely.

lines.text: `Collectors` supplies the recipes that gather a finished stream back into a collection, such as `toSet()` and `toList()`.
Extra Baker's Lane items are added so the vendor-specific pipelines later have more than one row to work on.
A `Set` is used because each vendor should appear only once, even though Sunny Fields Farm and Baker's Lane each sell several products.
Storing the vendor name in a variable means the same value drives the menu, the discount calculation, and the printed headings.
`forEach` walks the returned list and the method reference `System.out::println` prints each formatted menu line.
The discount is passed as a fraction, 0.10 meaning 10% off, so the same method could apply any discount.
Each task lives in its own small static method, which keeps `main` readable and lets you test the pipelines one at a time.
`map` replaces every product in the stream with just its vendor name, turning a stream of objects into a stream of strings.
Filtering after the map drops any missing or empty vendor names so they never reach the final set.
Collecting into a set discards duplicate vendor names automatically.
Only products from the requested vendor survive; `equalsIgnoreCase` means a difference in capitalization will not cause a miss.
This map builds a display string per product, with `%.2f` forcing exactly two decimal places so prices line up like currency.
Converting the discount into a multiplier once, outside the stream, avoids recomputing it for every element.
The price is scaled by the discount factor, and `Math.max` guards against a negative result if someone passes a discount above 100%.
